title: Hubbard, Turrentine and Benson: hit-making versus expressing feelings
summary: Sam judges Freddie Hubbard, Stanley Turrentine and George Benson by whether they aim for hits.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: What about George Benson? Freddie Hubbard, Stanley Turrentine?
Because they claim they are jazz fusion artists; that's what they mean--

Well Freddie, uh, have he backed out of that stuff. He does not choose to play it anymore. Which I, ah, ah, give him applause for that 'cause the man has a tremendous talent and he's one of my favorite trumpet players and I was glad to see him back out of that. Now, as for, who?
Well, Stanley Turrentine always was a commercial artist to me man. You know, he's a fine
musician and a beautiful ideals and he did a few things that I like. Ah, that blues he did with, ah, Ron--[Carter]

"Sugar", and which was a very exciting song. But, uh, and he's always been ah, a blues artist to me because that's all I heard from him, man. You know, I never heard anything else, I heard some things [Scott] him and Shirley used to do, with the organ group. Which was ah, ah musical, but he did things the only to, to ah, make hits. You know, there is a hit, it's two different kinds of things here man, there's a guy who's just concentrating on trying to make a hit record and then a guy who's just trying to express his feelings in in and try and play some music.
So, it's about attitude then, that's what you're saying, too, huh?
And the attitude of the individual is what they, what they intention is.

Exactly. And, and and what they're talent is too. OK, see, on top of that, you see. Now uh, it's like I said, Mr. Turrentine is uh, I think he is a fantastic saxaphone player but, um, I like him for what he does and what he can do. Now, what he's doing because, ah, I'm not all that impressed--but I never have, I never heard him do anthing else man. You know, now maybe he ah, you know--
I couldn't say man, because I never heard the man do anything else but commercial music, you see? Never heard nothing else.

George Benson is a fine ah, ah, guitarist, man. And uh, and uh, I guess he didn't know he could sing either. (Laughter). Jazz, you know. And uh, I guess just to waste some time he should have been doing that years ago, you know. And I'm also uh, happy to see him ---- better but I could listen, ah to guitar players, I would you know, --
